signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + BoJ Leaning
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.33, holding below its SMA200 at 158.48 while remaining above the SMA20/50 cluster at 157.65/157.71. Leveraged funds hold net short JPY at -30,379 contracts with pctl(52w) at 90 and a WoW reduction of -13,570 contracts, pointing to stretched short positioning vulnerable to squeezes. The options market heavily discounts upside follow-through: USD/JPY 1M 25d RR sits at -1.80, demonstrating strong put skew and demand for downside protection. Implied volatility at 7.9% runs below 30-day realized volatility of 9.7%, generating a negative vol risk premium of -1.8% that signals complacency in spot pricing. While headline flow indicates the BoJ leans against an immediate rate hike, the 264bp OIS carry advantage favors USD, anchoring the pair until US CPI prints. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside protection demand dominates despite carry support. Catalyst: US CPI report on 14 Oct. Risk: Core CPI beats expectations, forcing carry continuation toward 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Squeeze + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1204, pinned below its downward-sloping SMA20 at 1.1327 and SMA50 at 1.1492. Leveraged funds hold net short EUR at -84,775 contracts, sitting at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.64, representing a crowded speculative short. Options show elevated hedging demand with 1M implied volatility at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, creating a notable +2.3% vol risk premium. Retail positioning stands at 85% long, directly diverging from institutional CFTC net short positioning and creating two-way liquidation risk. Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a 135bp policy rate advantage favoring USD, alongside a +143bp OIS carry spread. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, policy divergence and retail extreme outweigh stretched spec shorts. Catalyst: US CPI release on 14 Oct. Risk: US core CPI prints at 0.1% or lower, triggering a short squeeze through SMA20 resistance at 1.1327.
evidence: Retail sentiment: 85% long vs CFTC institutional short

signals.title: NOK — G10 Outperformance + Restrictive Stance
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers NOK as the weekly outperformer with a 1W average gain of +0.535% across 2 pairs, exceeding the +0.50% threshold. Norges Bank policy rate sits at 4.5% with inflation expectations at 2.68%, producing a real policy rate of +1.82%, the most restrictive stance across the G10 complex. USD/NOK trades at 9.517, breaking below its SMA20 of 9.524 while holding above the SMA50 at 9.426. WTI crude oil advances +0.78% to $94.9, adding terms-of-trade support to the domestic currency. Domestic data confirms the trend, with the Economic Surprise Index showing a positive bias of +13.1. Trade bias: Bullish NOK, sustained by G10 outperformance and high real policy yields. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting on 5 Nov. Risk: WTI crude drops below $90.0, undermining terms of trade.
evidence: NOK real policy rate: +1.82% (policy 4.5% minus infl 2.68%)

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Compression + Yield Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3258, compressed tightly against its SMA20 at 1.3269, while remaining below the SMA50 and SMA200 cluster at 1.3431/1.3439. CFTC leveraged funds hold a modest net long position of +6,063 contracts, though 52-week percentile sits at 8 with z-score at -1.48, reflecting a recent large-scale liquidation over the past 4 weeks (-34,298 contracts). The 2Y sovereign yield spread vs US widened +26bp over the last 5 sessions to +2bp, providing short-term support to sterling. Fed 4.00% vs BoE 3.75% maintains a narrow 25bp policy rate advantage for the USD, mirrored by a +14bp OIS carry spread. MOVE Index at the 94th percentile vs VIX at the 16th percentile highlights rate market uncertainty that limits directional momentum. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD, technical compression between 1.3200 support and 1.3270 resistance. Catalyst: UK GDP m/m release at 06:00 UTC on 14 Oct. Risk: UK GDP contracts sharply, breaking range support at 1.3200.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoE 3.75% — 25bp carry favors USD
